slot.brief: Ratio of Bohr radii or energies of He+ vs H for the same n, or energy of an n-th level of a hydrogen-like ion; single scaling formula.

stem: The energy of the $n=2$ level of hydrogen is $-3.4$ eV. What is the energy of the $n=2$ level of $\text{He}^+$?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, energy scales as Z² at fixed n. He⁺ has Z=2, so E₂=4(−3.4 eV)=−13.6 eV.

working:
$E_n\propto -\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$
At the same $n$: $E_n(\text{He}^+)=4E_n(\text{H})$
$=4(-3.4)=-13.6\ \text{eV}$ Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, energy scales as Z² at fixed n. He⁺ has Z=2, so E₂=4(−3.4 eV)=−13.6 eV.
solution:
For a hydrogen-like ion, $E_n\propto -\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$. At the same $n$, He$^+$ has $Z=2$, so
$$E_2(\text{He}^+)=2^2E_2(\text{H})=4(-3.4)=-13.6\ \text{eV}.$$

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses the reciprocal scaling factor; B: Ignores the change in nuclear charge; C: Applies a factor of two instead of four.
